doc: The Sin-Eater (slug sin-eater) - slot 8 of the master-everyday-3 batch (THR-1840).

stakes.goal: eat a dead merchant's sins before his burial
stakes.risk: be called a forger before the whole parish
stakes.won: ate the merchant's sins and told the parish his crime
stakes.lost: was not believed, and the household set the watch
stakes.lostBadly: was called a forger before the whole parish

negative.won: ate the merchant's sins and buried his crime with him
negative.lost: left the merchant to be buried unclean
negative.lostBadly: left the merchant unclean, and the parish blamed them

template.name: The Sin-Eater

openings.urban: {actor} arrives in {location} at dusk, sent for by the parish.
openings.rural: {actor} comes to {location} at dusk, sent for by the parish.

steps.narrativeTemplate:
A rich wool merchant lies dead in his hall, to be buried at dawn. His eldest, {cast:eldest}, has paid for a sin-eater, so the merchant goes to the grave clean. Bread and salt lie on his chest.

{actor} must eat the bread and salt before the household and take every sin whole. A sin-eater who leaves a sin on the dead is not sent for again.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: {actor} ate the bread and salt to the last crumb, and the household saw the merchant go clean. Under the bread lay a folded paper in the merchant's own hand.
steps.successAfterimage: {actor} ate the bread and salt and took the sins whole. Under the bread lay a folded paper in the merchant's own hand.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: {actor} took the sins whole, but choked on the salt in front of the household. Under the bread lay a folded paper in the merchant's own hand.
steps.failureAfterimage: {actor} could not finish the bread, and the household saw a sin left on the dead. Under the bread lay a folded paper in the merchant's own hand.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: {actor} put the bread down half-eaten, and {cast:eldest} sent them out of the hall.

nudges.name: Seal The Lips
nudges.effectLine: Lay a vow of silence on them. They lean toward keeping what they learn hidden.

bandProse.success: {actor} ate in silence and kept their eyes on the bread.
bandProse.success_at_cost: {actor} ate in such silence that the household grew uneasy.
bandProse.failure: {actor} kept silent so long that the household thought the rite had stalled.

nudges.name: Stir The Conscience
nudges.effectLine: Make any wrong they learn sit heavy on them. They lean toward carrying it to the people it harmed.

bandProse.critical_success: {actor} ate every crumb, then read the paper under it twice.
bandProse.near_miss: {actor} named the sins aloud as the rite asks, but stumbled on the last.
bandProse.failure: {actor} stopped eating to read the paper, and the household saw bread left on the dead.
bandProse.critical_failure: {actor} read the paper aloud in the hall before the bread was finished.

positive.narrativeTemplate:
The paper is a confession. Years ago the merchant poisoned his partner and took the business. The partner's heir, {cast:wronged}, still keeps a stall in the market and has never known.

{actor} will not bury it. They carry the paper to {cast:wronged} and read it before the parish priest at the lych-gate. The household calls it a forgery, written by a sin-eater who wants paying twice. {actor} must make the parish believe the dead man's own words.
positive.criticalSuccessAfterimage: The priest knew the merchant's hand and said so at the lych-gate. {cast:wronged} heard every word.
positive.successAfterimage: The parish believed the paper, and {cast:wronged} heard how the partner died.
positive.successAtCostAfterimage: The parish believed the paper, but the household swore at the lych-gate that {actor} had forged it.
positive.failureAfterimage: The parish would not take a dead man's paper from a sin-eater's hand.
positive.criticalFailureAfterimage: The household tore the paper from {actor}'s hand at the lych-gate, and the parish took their side.

critical_success.text: They took every sin, and the household saw it.

success_at_cost.text: The household saw them choke on the salt.

near_miss.text: They took the sins, but slowly.

failure.text: A sin is still on the dead man.

effects.narrativeHook: Found a poisoning hidden under a dead man's bread, and wants to know what else the rich have hidden.

nudges.name: Wake Old Grief
nudges.effectLine: Bring a past loss back to the listeners, so they ask again how it happened.

bandProse.critical_success: The old men at the lych-gate remembered how sudden the partner's death was, and asked how it came.
bandProse.success: The parish remembered how fast the partner had died.
bandProse.failure: The parish remembered the partner, and remembered the merchant's alms to the poor as well.
bandProse.critical_failure: The parish remembered only the merchant's alms, and turned on {actor}.

nudges.name: Steady The Voice
nudges.effectLine: Keep their speech level and slow, so each word carries to the back of a crowd.

bandProse.success: {actor} read the paper slowly, and the back of the crowd heard it.
bandProse.near_miss: {actor} read steadily, but the household shouted over the last lines.
bandProse.failure: {actor} read every word steadily, and the parish still did not believe.

negative.narrativeTemplate:
The paper is a confession. Years ago the merchant poisoned his partner and took the business.

{actor} keeps it, as a sin-eater should: a sin eaten is a sin buried. At the lych-gate, {cast:wronged}, the partner's heir, stops the bier and asks before the parish what was on the dead man's chest. {actor} must see the merchant into the ground clean, and tell the parish no lie.
negative.criticalSuccessAfterimage: {actor} said the sins were eaten and buried, and the parish said amen. {actor} burned the paper at the graveside.
negative.successAfterimage: {actor} told {cast:wronged} the sins were eaten and buried, and the merchant went into the ground clean.
negative.successAtCostAfterimage: {cast:wronged} left the lych-gate sure the sin-eater had been paid for silence.
negative.failureAfterimage: {actor} stumbled on the burial words, and the parish said the merchant went down unclean.
negative.criticalFailureAfterimage: {actor} lost the burial words at the graveside, and the parish blamed the sin-eater.

critical_success.text: They took every sin, and the household saw it.

success_at_cost.text: The household saw them choke on the salt.

near_miss.text: They took the sins, but slowly.

failure.text: A sin is still on the dead man.

effects.narrativeHook: Carries a poisoner's sin, and is driven to set it right by work for others.

nudges.name: Ease The Dead
nudges.effectLine: Settle a restless spirit toward rest, so the burial rite closes without a fault.

bandProse.critical_success: The bearers carried the bier through the lych-gate without a stop.
bandProse.success: The burial rite closed without a fault.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The rite closed, but only after the bearers stopped twice at the gate.
bandProse.failure: The rite closed, and the bearers swore the bier grew heavy at the gate.

nudges.name: Soften Hard Words
nudges.effectLine: Cool an angry questioner's temper, so the questions come quieter and fewer.

bandProse.success: {cast:wronged} asked once, heard the answer, and stood aside.
bandProse.near_miss: {cast:wronged} stood aside, but asked twice first.
bandProse.critical_failure: {cast:wronged} asked so quietly that the whole parish leaned in to hear.

traitVariants.factorLine: Being Patient, they eat slowly and leave no crumb.
Being False, they are not trusted with a dead man's sins.

template.description: A rich merchant lies dead, and his household has paid for his sins to be eaten before the burial. Under the bread on his chest is his own written confession to a poisoning, and the sin-eater has to decide whether it goes into the grave with him.
